We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps correspond to forward reactions: 1) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) amide coupling (carboxylic acid + amine). So retrosynthesis: break target into three precursors.

Target: a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide (C= C - C(=O)N- aniline). Actually structure: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl which has side chain /C=C/C(=O)N- aniline (anilide). So retrosynthesis steps:

Step 1 (reverse of sulfonamide formation): disconnect S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) and aniline? Actually sulfonamide formed from amine (the p-tolyl amine) reacting with sulfonyl chloride derived from the other phenyl sulfonyl group. In target, the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the p-tolyl ring (aniline) and sulfonyl attached to second phenyl ring (with side chain). So retrosynthetic disconnection: break S-N bond to give p-toluidine (para-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride of the second phenyl (p-...?). The sulfonyl chloride would be: ClSO2-Ph-... with side chain attached to phenyl (the same phenyl bearing the unsaturated amide). So precursor 1: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1). Precursor 2: sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2.

Step 2 (reverse of Doebner modification): The α,β-unsaturated acid side chain is formed from aldehyde + malonic acid. In target, we have α,β-unsaturated amide after coupling, but before amide coupling we have α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl: /C=C/C(=O)OH? Actually after step 2 we have unsaturated acid attached to phenyl: phenyl-CH=CH-COOH. Then step 3 couples with aniline (c3ccccc3N) to form amide. So we need to disconnect amide bond: break C(=O)-N to give carboxylic acid (phenyl-CH=CH-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step 3 reverse: amide coupling.

Thus retrosynthesis:

Target -> (1) sulfonamide disconnection -> p-toluidine + sulfonyl chloride (with unsaturated acid side chain). Then sulfonyl chloride -> (2) from phenyl sulfonyl chloride precursor? Actually sulfonyl chloride is derived from phenyl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-...). That phenyl has side chain unsaturated acid. So we need to generate that phenyl sulfonyl chloride from phenyl sulfonic acid? But we have only 3 steps total, so step 2 is Doebner modification to create the unsaturated acid side chain on that phenyl. Starting material for step 2 would be aldehyde attached to phenyl (para? Actually the phenyl bearing sulfonyl group). The aldehyde would be p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl ring; the side chain is attached to same phenyl ring at para position relative to sulfonyl? In SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. So the phenyl ring (c2ccc...cc2) has the unsaturated amide at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: S(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So sulfonyl attached to phenyl at position 1, side chain at position 4 (para). So the aldehyde precursor for Doebner would be the same phenyl with aldehyde at para position: c2ccc(C=O)cc2 attached to sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl chloride attaches to phenyl via S, not via carbon. So the phenyl ring is attached to sulfonyl group; the aldehyde would be on same phenyl ring (para). So precursor: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2 (para-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride). Then Doebner with malonic acid gives unsaturated acid (para-CH=CH-COOH) attached to phenyl sulfonyl chloride. That's step 2.

Thus overall three steps:

Step A (retro): target -> p-toluidine + sulfonyl chloride (para-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride after step 2? Actually after step 2 we have unsaturated acid, not aldehyde. So we need to go further back: sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated acid (product of Doebner). So step 1: break sulfonamide to give p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated acid.

Step 2: break unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid (Doebner). So sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde (para-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride) is precursor.

Step 3: break amide bond to give aniline (c3ccccc3N) and carboxylic acid (the unsaturated acid). Wait amide bond is between unsaturated acid and aniline. In step 2 we already have unsaturated acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl chloride. So step 3 is amide coupling: unsaturated acid + aniline -> unsaturated amide (which is part of target). But we already used amide coupling in forward direction after Doebner? Actually forward order: Doebner (aldehyde + malonic acid) -> unsaturated acid. Then amide coupling (unsaturated acid + aniline) -> unsaturated amide. Then sulfonamide formation (p-toluidine + sulfonyl chloride (which already contains unsaturated amide attached) ) -> final product. So retrosynthesis order: target -> break sulfonamide -> get sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated amide + p-toluidine. Then break amide -> get unsaturated acid + aniline. Then break unsaturated acid via Doebner -> aldehyde + malonic acid (malonic acid is simple). So final precursors: p-toluidine, aniline, malonic acid, and para-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait the aldehyde is para-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride, which includes the sulfonyl chloride group. So we need that as a precursor. So total distinct precursors: p-toluidine (C), aniline (c3ccccc3N), malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH), and para-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CHO). That's four, but we have three reactions, okay.

Now we need to find template IDs for each reaction type.

We need to search for sulfonamide formation template (break S-N). Use search with functional_groups_broken maybe "sulfonamides" and formed "sulfonyl chloride, primary amine". Let's get list of functional groups.
